present_on_scene_date.note: PRESENCE ON THE SCENE DATE IS AN ASSUMPTION OF CONTINUITY AND NOT A STATEMENT. Nothing reached follows this household past 1833. It is graded uncertain rather than present because the town's population roughly quadrupled between the roster and the scene date and a great many of the men on it were, in Andreas's own phrase, 'adventurers, comprising moneyed speculators and prospectors, as yet undecided whether to stay at Chicago or go on'.

persons.name: E. H. Mulford
persons.note: Andreas vol. 1, printed p. 132 (scan p. 281), 'an imperfect list of the denizens of the town in the fall of 1833, not before named'. It gives a name, a trade and usually an arrival year, and it is a retrospective of 1884: a YEAR off it is documented, a MONTH is not, and it says nothing whatever about 1835.

resident_research.evidence_for: The current E. H. Mulford watchmaker record conflicts with stronger same-period evidence: the project's July/August 1835 Chicago Democrat corpus prints J. H. Mulford in watches and jewelry, while later directories distinguish Major E. H. Mulford from James H. and Edward H. Jr. The household may conflate members of the Mulford family, so no automatic rename or relationship is asserted.
resident_research.evidence_against: Existing Andreas-derived record says E. H. Mulford and arrival 1833; later sources distinguish multiple Mulford men in the jewelry business.
resident_research.notes: The current E. H. Mulford watchmaker record conflicts with stronger same-period evidence: the project's July/August 1835 Chicago Democrat corpus prints J. H. Mulford in watches and jewelry, while later directories distinguish Major E. H. Mulford from James H. and Edward H. Jr. The household may conflate members of the Mulford family, so no automatic rename or relationship is asserted.

research_note: THE ONLY WATCHMAKER IN THE DATASET, and a trade that says something about the town the buildings do not: a settlement supports a watchmaker only when enough people own watches and enough of them break. Andreas's later lists carry an E. H. Mulford sworn in a county proceeding, which corroborates the man's continuing residence at some later date and does not reach 1835.
